subject: Security notice: request for response matrix and contract extracts
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@finvault.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finvault.com
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security notice: request for response matrix and contract extracts

Hi Ben / Kimberly,

We discovered an anomalous export attempt in one of our sandbox buckets that may have touched logs containing customer identifiers. We do not have confirmation of exfiltration yet but procurement/security want to confirm contractual obligations and Redwood's notification commitments while we triage.

Could you share: 1) a short incident response matrix that shows who we should contact at Redwood for first notice / evidence export / legal requests (name, role, phone/email) and 2) the exact contract extracts that describe Redwood's incident notification timeline, scope, and obligations to cooperate with forensic requests (we need the snippet to present to our counsel).

We appreciate an ETA; procurement would like something for our internal review by EOD Wednesday if possible.

Thanks,
Julie Park
Security Operations
FinVault

Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@finvault.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security notice: request for response matrix and contract extracts

Julie — thanks for the heads up and sorry you're dealing with this. We're standing up a quick internal kick-off to pull the materials.

Short answers up front:
- We'll provide a one-page contact/response matrix (first notice, forensics lead, legal escalation) within 24 business hours.
- We'll extract the incident-notification and data-transfer clauses from your current SOW/DPA and send annotated snippets for counsel review.

Kimberly / Marissa: can you own the contract snippet and statutory notice language? Grace, can you prepare the contact matrix with direct lines and escalation order?

Julie — can you confirm whether FinVault classifies this as an "incident triggering the 48-hour notification clause" under your counsel's view, or if this is an "investigatory event" for now? That helps us prioritize the forensic packaging.

Ben

Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security notice: request for response matrix and contract extracts

Hi all — taking point on contract excerpts. I pulled the DPA and highlighted the relevant sections. Key call-outs:

- Notification timing: our standard DPA sets a "best reasonable effort" to notify within 72 hours of becoming aware of a confirmed breach; for confirmed incidents involving regulated data there is an escalated 48-hour target that requires coordination with our legal team and relevant subprocessors.

- Scope: Redwood's obligation to notify covers Customer Data that is reasonably likely to have been accessed or disclosed; telemetry/operational logs that are fully anonymized are out of scope unless they contain identifiers.

- Cooperation: we commit to provide reasonable assistance (forensic snapshots, access to relevant logs, exportable evidence) subject to legal/process checks and any export/regulatory constraints. We do not provide raw customer data dumps without a court order or mutually agreed escrow arrangement.

I attached an annotated PDF with the exact clause snippets for counsel. Marissa — please confirm if we should soften the 72h language to 96h for this customer given their procurement stance, or keep the standard language and offer a service credit in the SOW.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: contract-extracts.pdf (pdf, annotated excerpts)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@finvault.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security notice: request for response matrix and contract extracts

Julie / Ben / team — legal + procurement here. A couple of operational clarifications:

- For cross-border evidence requests we need to confirm export authority from the FinVault side (POC: procurement@finvault.com). If FinVault wants raw forensic exports crossing EU/UK/US boundaries we must map subprocessors and confirm contractual transfer mechanisms.

- On timing: Kimberly's summary is accurate. We typically say 72 hours for internal confirmation and 48 hours for regulatory-notifiable incidents only when the facts are clear. Given the uncertainty you described, propose we supply the response matrix and the clause extracts now, and offer a forensic snapshot package within 5 business days — faster if the case escalates to confirmed breach status.

- Marissa (commercial) note: to meet procurement's request for a quicker commitment, we can offer an optional SOW addendum that guarantees a 48-hour notification SLA for an additional monitoring/forensics retainer. That buys them the faster timeline and limits our exposure.

Grace — can you attach the contact matrix as an Excel (include pager/esc coverage)?

Marissa Cole
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-response-matrix.xlsx (contact + escalation order)

1) Procurement will review the clause snippets and come back with any redlines by Friday.
2) Security will continue triage; we will update you if we move from investigatory event to confirmed incident.
3) We'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk the response matrix and clarify export constraints (Alan from CloudMarket will join re: subprocessor routing).

Appreciate the clarity on the optional addendum; we'll surface that to procurement.

Julie Park

FinVault
